cells.tense: You are holding two living things up at once and neither one is tipping today.
cells.ask: Hand the small daily tasks to someone else for one afternoon, and let what you tend get along at its own speed while you are gone.
cells.core:
You are tending two growing things and keeping both in good shape, without making a show of it. You know what each one needs and roughly when. That kind of steadiness runs so quietly it looks like nothing is happening, which is exactly what it looks like from the inside.

You are not hovering and you are not letting go. You check the soil, you wait, you adjust one small thing and then leave it alone. People around you feel the difference even when they cannot name it. Keep the same hand. Hold the middle a while longer. Nothing here needs to change today.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding two things up and neither one is tipping.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: in the conditions where something is coming along

cells.tense: You will be standing over what you love, pulling a future toward you before it has grown into itself.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are tending and leave it alone today unless it asks. Let it come to you, or not.
cells.core:
You can see where this is going, and you are already living there. You check on it more than it needs, you fix what has not gone wrong, you picture the finished version and hold today against it. The care is doing its job. Push is doing its job too, and push is what costs you the very thing you want most.

Done right, this is simple: you make the conditions, you keep them right, and then you step back far enough that the thing can stand without you. You have done the hard part. What is left is waiting, and waiting is the piece you keep skipping because the outcome matters too much to leave it be.
cells.sheetLine: You are steering what grows instead of letting it grow.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: in the conditions where something is coming along

cells.tense: Something you were tending got left behind, and you have not walked back toward it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have set down and give it ten minutes of plain attention today, not fixing, just looking at it.
cells.core:
There is something you were looking after, and the looking-after has gone quiet. Not dead. You can still feel it sitting there. But you stopped showing up to it, and the habit of reaching for it wore thin without your catching it.

You did not decide to stop. It stopped the way a garden stops when nobody walks past it. The way back is small. You show up with no occasion and do one plain thing for it. Then again the next day. Pick up one small piece today and let that be the whole job. Not to prove anything. You are only walking past it again.
cells.sheetLine: You set it down and have not walked back yet.

cells.tense: You are the reason something around you is doing well, and you keep saying it is fine on its own.
cells.ask: Tell one person, plainly: 'I kept that alive.' Just the sentence, nothing after it, and let them hear it.
cells.core:
Something near you is growing and you are the one who made that possible. The timing, the small adjustments, the days you showed up when nobody watched. You talk about it like it happened on its own, or like anyone would have done the same. Anyone would not have.

You have been calling your part background while it did the actual work. When someone thanks you, you wave it off. Read it right and the move is plain: a person names what they did and lets it stand. Your hand is in there, and you have not said so once, out loud, to anyone. That is a real thing you did. Someone should hear it from you.
cells.sheetLine: You kept it alive and you call that nothing.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is already 'the one deciding what gets tended' — the record shows capacity, not authorship claimed. A reader could reasonably say: 'I'm not deciding anything, I'm just keeping things alive.' The ask survives being wrong because handing the small odds and ends to someone else still shows them where their own hand was. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line about how much they're carrying unacknowledged; cut that.
